Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:1.english: [Are] terumah - Because permitted growths do not neutralize the prohibition.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:2.hebrew: בגידולי גידולין קאמר - דהכי קאמר: גידולי בצל של תרומה שנטעה, ורבו גידוליו על עיקרו, דהוו להו גידולי גידולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:2.english: Of the growths of growths he says - For this is what he means: the growths of an onion of teruma that one planted, and its growths exceeded its original [part], such that they are growths of growths.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:3.english: We learned, etc. - That the growths of growths of teruma [are] non-sacred.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:4.hebrew: אפי' בדבר שאין זרעו כלה - כגון בצל, גידולי גידולין מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:1:4.english: Even in something whose seed does not cease - For example, an onion — [its] growths of growths are permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:2:1.hebrew: בדבר שזרעו כלה - כגון חיטים. גידולי גידולין — דזהו השני:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:2:1.english: In an item whose seed ceases - Such as wheat. Growths of growths — for this is the second [growth].

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:2:2.hebrew: תריץ רבויא של גידולי גידולין דרבו גידוליו על עיקרו מותר קא משמע לן - כלומר, הא אתא לאשמועינן: גידולי גידולין של בצל של תרומה ורבו אותן גידולין על עיקרו — מותר, דזהו השלישי:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:2:2.english: [The Gemara] answered: The increase of the growths of growths, [that is,] where its growths exceeded its primary [part], is permitted — [this is what] it teaches us - That is to say, this is what it comes to teach us: [in the case of] growths of growths of an onion of terumah, where those growths exceeded its primary [part], it is permitted — for this is the third [growth].

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:1.english: Konam wine that I taste today - For [this] implies as long as it is day, and no more.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:2.hebrew: שבת זו - והיה עומד בשבת, אסור בכל השבת — בששת ימי השבוע:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:2.english: This week - [If] he was standing during the week, he is prohibited for the entire week — [that is,] the six days of the week.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:3.hebrew: והשבת שעברה - כלומר, בשבת שהוא עומד בה. ולהכי קרי ליה שעברה, לפי שהשבת זה אינו מתחשב אחר ימים הבאים, אלא אחר ששת ימים שעברו:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:3.english: And the Shabbat that passed - That is to say, on the Shabbat [of the week] in which he is standing. And this is why [the Mishnah] calls it "that passed": because this Shabbat is not reckoned after the coming days, but rather after the six days that passed.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:4.hebrew: חדש זה - אמר קונם יין שאיני שותה בזה החדש, והיה עומד באותו יום של ר"ח:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:4.english: This month - [If] he said, "Wine is konam [to me] that I will not drink in this month," and he was standing on that day of Rosh Chodesh.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:5.english: Prohibited for the entire month - For all the coming thirty days.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:6.hebrew: וראש חדש להבא - כלומר, ר"ח זה שהוא עומד לתוכו, הוא נמנה עם ימים הבאים, שהוא ראשון שלהם:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:4:6.english: And the New Moon is for the coming [month] - That is to say, this New Moon that he is entering into is counted with the coming days, for it is the first of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:5:1.hebrew: וכן אם היה עומד בראש השנה ואמר קונם יין שאיני טועם שנה זו - אסור בכל השנה ואותו היום של ראש השנה שהוא עומד בו. ולהכי קרי לעתיד לבא, לפי שהוא נמנה לימים ולחדשים הנכנסים, שהוא אחר זמן, ולהכי קאמר לעתיד ולא קאמר להבא:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:5:1.english: And similarly, if he was standing on Rosh Hashanah and said, "Konam, wine that I will not taste this year" - [He is] prohibited for the entire year, and [on] that day of Rosh Hashanah on which he is standing. And that is why [the Mishnah] calls [it] "for the future to come," because it is counted with the incoming days and months, which are after [some] time; and that is why it says "for the future" and does not say "for the coming [period]."

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:5:2.hebrew: ואם היה עומד בשנת השמיטה ואמר קונם יין שאיני טועם בשבוע זו, אסור בכל השבוע הבא - ואותה שנה שביעית שהוא עומד בה נמנית לשבוע שעברה, להכי קרי ליה ״שעברה״:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:5:2.english: And if he was standing in the Sabbatical year and said, "Konam, wine that I will not taste [during] this seven-year cycle," he is prohibited for the entire upcoming seven-year cycle - And that seventh year in which he is standing is counted with the seven-year cycle that passed; that is why [the Mishnah] calls it "that passed."

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:6:1.hebrew: ואם אמר - שאיני טועם יום אחד — מעת לעת, שאם היה עומד בשעת הנדר בחצי היום, אסור למחר עד חצי היום. וכן אם אמר שבת אחד, באיזה יום שעומד בשבוע, אסור עד יום שמיני לאותו יום שנדר. וכן בשנה אחת וכן בשבוע אחת — אסור שנה שלימה ושבוע שלם מיום ליום:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:6:1.english: And if he said - "I will not taste [wine for] one day," [he is prohibited] for a full twenty-four-hour period, for if he was standing at midday at the time of the vow, he is prohibited until midday the next day. And similarly, if he said "one week," on whatever day of the week he is [when he vows], he is prohibited until the eighth day from that day on which he vowed. And similarly with "one year," and similarly with "one seven-year cycle" — he is prohibited for a complete year or a complete seven-year cycle, from day to day.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:7:1.english: [If] one said, "Konam, wine that I will not taste until Passover," it is forbidden until [Passover] arrives - according to all [opinions].

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:7:2.english: "Until it will be" — [it is] forbidden until it ends - For it implies that he meant until all of Passover passes.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:7:3.english: Until before Passover - It implies until [Passover] arrives, and it implies until [it] ends.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:7:4.hebrew: עד שיגיע - דקסבר לא מעייל איניש נפשיה לספיקא:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:7:4.english: Until it arrives - For he holds a person does not bring himself [into doubt].

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:8:1.hebrew: לכשתחשך - אע"פ שעבר היום:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:8:1.english: When darkness falls - Even though the day has passed.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:8:2.english: [He] requires asking a sage - to dissolve his vow for him, for the sake of a distinction.

Rashi on Nedarim 60a:9:1.hebrew: גזירה היום אטו יום אחד - דאי אמרת לכשתחשך, אע"פ שעבר היום, הוי מותר, אתו למימר נמי כי נדר יום אחד ועומד בחצי היום מותר לכשתחשך, ואיהו לא הוי מותר עד מעת לעת. הילכך, צריך שאלה לחכם; וכיון דבעי שאלה לחכם, חכם חוקר כיצד נדר, ולא יבא לידי חילול נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 60a:9:1.english: A decree [concerning] "today" due to "one day" - For if you say [that] when it gets dark — even though the day has passed — he becomes permitted, [people] will also come to say [that] when one vowed [for] "one day" and is standing in the middle of the day, he is permitted when it gets dark, whereas he is not permitted until a twenty-four-hour period [has elapsed]. Therefore, he requires a request [for dissolution] to a Sage; and since he requires a request to a Sage, the Sage investigates how he vowed, and he will not come to desecrate [his] vow.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:1:1.english: Of the growths of growths - [This refers to a case] like this, where the onion itself was growths of terumah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:1:2.hebrew: ה"ג התם דלא רבו הכא דרבו - פירוש: הא דאמר "גידולי גידולין אסורין" גבי טבל, היינו כל כמה דלא רבו גידולי גידולין על העיקר; אבל הכא ברבו, הלכך מבטלי גידולין לעיקר. ובספרים כתוב: "ריבויא דרבו גידולין על עיקרו מותר קמ"ל". ויש לפרש כדפרישית, דמלתא דרבי חנינא מיירי דרבו גידולין על עיקרו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:1:2.english: We read the text as: "There, where they did not exceed [the principal]; here, where they did exceed [the principal]" - Explanation: That which it says, "the growths of growths are forbidden" regarding tevel [untithed produce], that is as long as the growths of growths did not exceed the principal; but here [it is a case] where they exceeded [it], therefore the growths nullify the principal. And in [other] texts it is written: "It teaches us [regarding] an increase, where growths exceeded its principal, [that] it is permitted." And one can explain [this reading] as I explained earlier, that the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina deals with [a case] where the growths exceeded its principal.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:1:3.hebrew: קמשמע לן רבי חנינא דאפילו דבר שאין זרעו כלה, גידולי גידולין חולין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:1:3.english: Rabbi Chanina teaches us that even [in the case of] something whose seed does not cease, the growths of growths are non-sacred [produce].

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:2:1.hebrew: והתנן הטבל גידוליו מותרין לאכול אכילת ארעי בלא מעשר בדבר שזרעו כלה - כגון חיטין, אבל דבר שאין זרעו כלה, גידולי גידולין תרומה כמו טבל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:2:1.english: "But didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]: Untithed produce [tevel], its growths are permitted to be eaten as a casual meal without tithing, in [the case of] something whose seed ceases" - For example, wheat; but [for] something whose seed does not cease, the growths of growths are [treated as] terumah, like tevel.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:2:2.hebrew: ה"ג: התם דלא רבו, הכא דרבו - פירוש: הא דאמר "גידולי גידולין אסורין" גבי טבל — היינו כל כמה דלא רבו גידולי גידולין על העיקר, אבל הכא ברבו, הלכך מבטלי גידולין לעיקר. ובספרים כתוב: "ריבויא דרבו גידולין על עיקרו מותר קמ"ל", ויש לפרש כדפרישית, דמלתא דרבי חנינא מיירי דרבו גידולין על עיקרו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:2:2.english: We read [the text]: "There, where they did not exceed; here, where they exceeded" - Explanation: That which it says, "the growths of growths are forbidden," with regard to untithed produce [tevel] — that is as long as the growths of growths did not exceed the primary [part]; but here, [where] they exceeded [it], therefore the growths nullify the primary [part]. And in [some] books it is written: "It teaches us that [if] the increase of the growths exceeded its primary [part], [it is] permitted," and one can explain [it] as I explained [above], that Rabbi Chanina's statement refers to [a case] where the growths exceeded its primary [part].

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:1.english: "Wine is [forbidden as] a konam, etc., that I taste today, he is prohibited only until nightfall" - And it does not say that he is prohibited for a twenty-four-hour period, as in the latter clause [of the Mishnah] where he said "one day."

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:2.hebrew: שבת זו - ועומד באמצע, ביום ג' או ביום ד', אסור בכל השבת. כלומר: כל ימי אותה השבוע עד סופה. ושבת שעברה, כלומר: ושבת הבא עליו סוף השבוע אסור כמו כן, דאף השבת משבוע שעבר. ובגמ' פריך: פשיטא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:2.english: "This week" - And he is standing in the middle [of the week], on Tuesday or Wednesday; he is prohibited for the entire week, meaning all the days of that week until its end. "And [the] Shabbat that passed" — meaning, and the Shabbat coming upon him [at] the end of the week is likewise prohibited, for Shabbat too is [considered part] of the week that passed. And in the Gemara it asks: "[That is] obvious!"

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:3.hebrew: חדש זה - ועומד בט"ו ימים בטבת, אסור בכל החדש עד סופו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:3.english: "This month" - And [if] he is standing on the fifteenth day of Tevet, he is prohibited [from wine] for the entire month until its end.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:4.hebrew: ור"ח להבא - פי': ר"ח שבט של אחריו, היינו כלהבא ומותר בו, שהוא [מחדש] הבא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:4:4.english: And the New Moon [belongs] to the next [month] - Explanation: the New Moon of Shevat that follows it is [considered] like the next [month], and he is permitted [to drink wine] on it, since it is [from the] next [month].

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:5:1.hebrew: שבוע זה אסור בכל השבוע - ועומד הוא באמצע השמיטה, בשנה רביעית או חמישית לשמיטה — אסור עד סוף השבוע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:5:1.english: "This seven-year cycle — he is prohibited for the entire seven-year cycle" - And [suppose] he is standing in the middle of the Sabbatical cycle, in the fourth or fifth year of the Sabbatical cycle — he is prohibited until the end of the seven-year cycle.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:5:2.hebrew: והשביעית שעברה - כלומר, שנה השביעית הבאה היא כלשעבר, שנמנית עם שמיטה שעברה, ואסור בה; פי' זה רהוט. וי"מ: "שבת זו" — ועומד ביום שבת, ונודר "בשבת זו", אסור בכל השבת, כלומר בכל השבוע הבאה; "ושבת שעברה", כלומר ויום השבת שהוא נודר בו גם הוא אסור, ואע"פ שאמת הוא שהוא משבוע שעבר, הואיל ונדר בו אסור. ובגמרא פריך: פשיטא! "חדש זה" — ועומד בראש חדש, אסור בכל החדש, ור"ח שהוא בו כלהבא, כלומר אותו ר"ח שנודר בו אסור, ולכך קרי ליה להבא, שהוא עם ראש חדש הבא. וכן גבי ראש השנה, נמנה משנה הבאה; לכך קרי ליה להבא, לפי שהוא נמנה משנה הבאה. "שנה זו" — ועומד בראש השנה. "שבוע זו" — ועומד בשנה שביעית, אסור בכל השבוע, "ובשביעית שעברה", כלומר אע"פ שהיא מלשעבר, אסור בה כיון שנודר בה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:5:2.english: "And the Sabbatical year that passed" - That is to say, the coming seventh year is [considered] as of the past, for it is counted with the Sabbatical cycle that passed, and he is prohibited during it; this explanation is straightforward. And some explain: "[If he vows,] 'this Shabbat'" — [meaning] he is standing on the day of Shabbat and vows "this Shabbat" — he is prohibited for the entire Shabbat [i.e., week], that is to say, for the entire coming week; "and the Shabbat that passed," that is to say, the day of Shabbat on which he vows is also prohibited, and even though it is true that it belongs to the past week, since he vowed on it, it is prohibited. And in the Gemara it asks: Is that not obvious?! [The Gemara answers that it speaks of where he says,] "This month" — and he is standing on Rosh Chodesh: he is prohibited for the entire month, and the Rosh Chodesh on which he is [standing] is [considered] as the future, that is to say, that Rosh Chodesh on which he vows is prohibited, and therefore [the Mishnah] calls it "the future," because it is [counted] with the coming Rosh Chodesh. And similarly regarding Rosh HaShanah, it is counted with the coming year; therefore it calls it "the future," because it is counted with the coming year. "This year" — [this applies] when he is standing on Rosh HaShanah. "This seven-year cycle" — [this applies] when he is standing in the seventh year: he is prohibited for the entire seven-year cycle, "and in the Sabbatical year that passed," that is to say, even though it is from the past [cycle], he is prohibited during it since he vows during it:

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:6:1.hebrew: מיום ליום - כלומר, עד שנה אחרת באותו יום, וכן בשבוע אחרת לאותו יום שנדר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:6:1.english: "From day to day" - That is to say, until another year on that same day, and similarly in another seven-year cycle until that same day [on which] he vowed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:1.hebrew: הנודר עד הפסח אסור עד שיגיע - דבלשון בני אדם עד ולא עד בכלל, לכך אינו אסור אלא עד שיגיע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:1.english: One who vows "until Passover" is forbidden until it arrives - Because in human parlance, "until" [means] up to, and not inclusive [of the endpoint]; therefore, he is forbidden only until it arrives.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:2.hebrew: עד פני הפסח ר' מאיר אומר עד שיגיע - דה"ק: עד לפני יום של פסח:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:2.english: "Until before Passover, Rabbi Meir says: until it arrives" - For this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: until before the day of Passover.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:3.hebrew: ר' יוסי אומר עד שיצא - דשמא ה"ק: עד פני שעה אחרונה של יום אחרון של פסח — דסבר דמחית אינש נפשיה לספקא, ושמא נתכוון לומר פני שעה אחרונה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:7:3.english: Rabbi Yosei says: [It is forbidden] until it ends - For perhaps this is what he is saying: "until before [lit. the face of] the last hour of the last day of Passover" — for [Rabbi Yosei] holds that a person places himself in a situation of uncertainty, and perhaps he intended to say "before the last hour."

Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:8:1.hebrew: אמר ר' ירמיה לכשתחשך צריך שאלה לחכם - ואינו מותר בלא שאלה, ואע"ג דמן הדין היה מותר שהרי הגיע זמנו — גזירה אטו היכא דאמר "יום אחד"; כלומר, אי שרי ליה כשאמר "היום" לכשתחשך, אתי למישרי כשאמר "יום אחד", ואז הוא אסור עד מעת לעת: א"ה דחייש לאיחלופי, ליגזר ביום אחד דליתסר אף כשהגיע מעת לעת עד הלילה — שאמר עד מעת לעת — משום "היום", ד"היום" הוא אסור עד הערב. ומשני: "היום" ב"יום אחד" מיחלף, ואתי למשרי כשנודר בבוקר ואומר "קונם יום אחד עלי" לכשתחשך, שסבור שקיים נדרו לפי שעבר יום אחד. אבל "יום אחד" ב"היום" לא מיחלף: אם נתיר לו כשאמר "יום אחד" באמצע היום כשיבא מעל"ע, לא יבא להתיר כשאמר "היום" באמצע היום, שעדיין לא שמר לא מע"ל ולא יום שלם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60a:8:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: When darkness falls, he requires an inquiry of a sage - And he is not permitted [to drink wine] without an inquiry; and even though by the letter of the law he would be permitted, since his [vow's] time has arrived, [it is] a rabbinic decree on account of a case where he said "one day" — that is to say, if we permit him when he said "today" as soon as darkness falls, he will come to permit [it] when he said "one day," whereas then he is forbidden for a full twenty-four-hour period. [The Gemara asks:] If so, that [Rav Yosef] is concerned about confusion, let [the Sages] decree regarding "one day" that he be forbidden even when twenty-four hours have arrived until nightfall — [even though] he said [only] until twenty-four hours — because of "today," since [with] "today" he is forbidden until evening! And [the Gemara] answers: "Today" can be confused with "one day," and he will come to permit [himself] when he vows in the morning and says, "Konam [be such-and-such] upon me for one day," as soon as darkness falls, because he thinks that he has fulfilled his vow since one day [i.e., the daytime] has passed. However, "one day" will not be confused with "today": if we permit him when he said "one day" in the middle of the day when twenty-four hours arrive, he will not come to permit [himself] when he said "today" in the middle of the day, since he has not yet observed either twenty-four hours or a full day.
